entities.name: Konrad III the Old
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Konrad III the Old, a scion of the Silesian Piast dynasty, held sway as the Duke of Oleśnica (Oels), Koźle (Cosel), and portions of Bytom (Beuthen) and Ścinawa (Steinau) from 1377 until his death on December 28, 1412. His reign, initially as co-ruler with his father Konrad II the Gray and then as sole duke from 1403, marked a period of relative stability within the complex feudal landscape of late medieval Silesia, which was then a crown land of the Kingdom of Bohemia. His ducal seat at Oleśnica served as a minor but strategically important center, navigating the political currents between the powerful Bohemian crown and various neighboring Polish and German principalities.

During his tenure, Konrad III focused on the internal consolidation of his fragmented territories, a common challenge for Silesian Piast dukes whose lands were frequently partitioned through inheritance. While no major military campaigns or grand architectural projects are directly attributed to him, his reign was crucial for maintaining the ducal line and the integrity of the Oleśnica principality. He engaged in the customary diplomatic and familial alliances of the era, notably marrying Judith of Masovia, a daughter of Duke Siemowit IV, thereby strengthening connections with the Polish Piasts of Masovia and ensuring a robust succession with five sons, all named Konrad.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Konrad III the Old's importance lies in his successful maintenance of the Oleśnica ducal line and its territories during a complex period, directly leading to the prominent "Konradid" generation of Silesian Piasts. His rule solidified regional power dynamics and dynastic continuity for the next century.
